ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL SYNTAX ERROR (fixed by T1): lines 468-472 used Python-style adjacent-string concatenation inside a JS object literal for 'ce2.results.fee_exempt_body'. This raised 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token, expected ","' at compile time and broke the entire /ai-tools/contribution-estimator route (and any lazy chunk importing it) with a full-page ErrorBoundary. Fixed by inserting explicit '+' operators between the three string fragments. Root cause: JS does NOT support Python's implicit adjacent-string concatenation.

Acceptance-criteria miss: the ce-result-hero-label data-testid is only present on PointHeadline (line 562). RangeHeadline and FeeExemptHeadline render the persona hero label but do NOT expose data-testid="ce-result-hero-label" (Range uses raw <div> at line 600; FeeExempt uses ce-fee-exempt-hero at line 585). The review spec says the hero label testid should read 'estimated weekly contribution' / '{name}'s ...' across all result paths, so QA harnesses can't target Range/FeeExempt via ce-result-hero-label. Text still renders correctly; only the testid is missing.

reports_routes.py lines 486/614/715/800/909 all call _ai_summary(facts, report.get('_persona_context')) with the same _persona_context ref, meaning any Failed report retry still uses stale persona if the user switched persona mid-generation. Low-risk given async lifetime, but worth noting.

Frontend usePersonaTier1 uses `Array.isArray(keys) ? keys.join('|') : ''` as the effect key (line 219). If a caller passes the array inline each render, the join is still stable, but it defeats React DevTools memoization insight — consider requiring callers to memo the keys array.

rca of the issue: CE-2 blank page RCA: E1 authored CE2_PERSONA_DEFAULTS['ce2.results.fee_exempt_body'] using three adjacent string literals wrapped in parens (Python idiom). JS parses `"str1" "str2"` as two separate expressions and expects a `,` between object properties, so Babel raised 'Unexpected token, expected ","' at line 470:8. The lazy chunk for /ai-tools/contribution-estimator therefore failed the entire route with a hot-reload compilation error and the ErrorBoundary fallback screen. Fix: change the three concatenated strings to use JS '+' operator explicitly. Repro: git-blame shows the exact PR that landed CE2_PERSONA_DEFAULTS; the same author (or a copy-paste from the backend Python registry.py TIER1_VARIANTS map) is the likely source, since backend/lib/persona/registry.py uses the exact same three-line adjacent-string pattern (valid in Python). Mitigation: add ESLint rule 'no-adjacent-string-literals' (custom) or `no-multi-str` + explicit review checklist item when porting Python copy dictionaries to JS.
